## Summary

Adds `--config-format` as a vLLM-parity CLI alias for the existing `--model-config-parser`. Closes part 1 of #28020.

Motivated by #28020, which asks for the vLLM-style Mistral invocation

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4 \
  --config-format mistral \
  --load-format mistral \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral
```

to work verbatim on SGLang. The three flags map as follows on today's `main`:

| Flag from the vLLM invocation | Status on `main` |
| --- | --- |
| `--load-format mistral` | Works — `LoadFormat.MISTRAL` branch is wired in `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py`; auto-detected by `_is_mistral_native_format()` when the checkpoint ships `params.json` + `consolidated*.safetensors` and no `model-*.safetensors`. |
| `--config-format mistral` | Same feature exists under a different name: `--model-config-parser mistral`. Users copy-pasting the vLLM command hit an unknown-flag error. |
| `--tokenizer-mode mistral` | Choices are `["auto", "slow"]`. Not implemented — deferred, see below. |

This PR is the small, safe half — the CLI alias. `--tokenizer-mode mistral` needs a `mistral_common.tokens.tokenizers.mistral.MistralTokenizer` adapter into the `PreTrainedTokenizer` API, which is a separate change with its own review surface. Will open the follow-up under the same issue.

## Approach

`config_format: Optional[str]` on `ServerArgs`, default `None`. If set at parse time, `_handle_config_format()` (new) reconciles it into `model_config_parser` before the dummy-model short-circuit in `__post_init__` — so a conflict is caught even for dummy/none models — and before `_handle_load_format`, which relies on `model_config_parser` being finalized.

Reconciliation rules:

1. `config_format=None` → no-op. `model_config_parser` retains whatever was passed (default `"auto"`).
2. Input normalized: `.strip().lower()`. `--config-format="  Mistral  "` and `--config-format=MISTRAL` both become `mistral`.
3. Empty / whitespace-only after normalization → treated as not passed (no-op). Prevents `--config-format=""` from silently producing an unregistered parser name.
4. `config_format=X`, `model_config_parser="auto"` → `model_config_parser = X`.
5. `config_format=X`, `model_config_parser=Y` (both explicit, different, comparison case-insensitive) → `ValueError`. Explicit-conflict errors are more useful than a silent last-wins winner. `"auto"` is compared as a literal value on the `config_format` side — `--config-format=auto` together with an explicit `--model-config-parser=hf` also raises.
6. `config_format=X`, `model_config_parser=X` → accepted (no-op after propagation).
7. Side effect: `config_format="mistral"` + `load_format="auto"` → sets `load_format = "mistral"`. Mirrors vLLM's behavior — users who pass only `--config-format mistral` (as several Mistral docs pages show) still get Mistral weight loading. Explicit non-`auto` `load_format` values are respected.

`config_format` is a separate field rather than an `Arg(aliases=["--config-format"])` on `model_config_parser` specifically so passing both flags with conflicting values raises rather than silently letting whichever appears last on the command line win. Documented inline.

## Peripheral

`get_config()` in `utils/hf_transformers/config.py` raises a `ValueError` for `model_config_parser not in ("auto", "hf")` when the input is a GGUF file. Updated that error message to mention `--config-format` alongside `--model-config-parser`, so users who hit it via the alias recognize the flag name.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py` gains `TestConfigFormatAlias` with twelve cases covering every reconciliation state above, plus a regression test that confirms `_handle_config_format()` runs before the dummy-model short-circuit (so `ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", config_format="mistral", model_config_parser="hf")` still raises).

Tests follow the existing `SimpleNamespace` + `ServerArgs._handle_config_format(ns)` pattern to isolate the alias logic from `prepare_server_args` side effects — the alternative of driving reconciliation via `prepare_server_args` would need a real Mistral checkpoint on disk to exercise the "config_format=mistral" propagation path, since the Mistral config parser downstream would otherwise fail on a non-Mistral model.

Registered under `base-a-test-cpu` (unchanged from the file's existing `register_cpu_ci`).

## Alternatives considered

- **Rename `--model-config-parser` → `--config-format` with a deprecation shim.** Rejected: breaking, and `model_config_parser` is a more descriptive name for SGLang's plugin registry — the vLLM name is only useful as a copy-paste target.
- **Silently prefer one flag on conflict.** Rejected: hides misconfigurations. Erroring makes the intended value explicit at server boot.
- **`Arg(aliases=["--config-format"])` on the existing field.** Rejected: silent last-wins semantics on conflict, no way to distinguish "user passed both flags with matching values" from "user only passed one." Separate field lets the reconciler see both intents.
- **Ship `--tokenizer-mode mistral` in the same PR.** Rejected: the real work is adapting `mistral_common.MistralTokenizer` (or a similar direct load path) into `get_tokenizer()`, which is bigger than a CLI alias and worth its own review. Filed as follow-up.

## Follow-up

- `--tokenizer-mode mistral` — separate PR, will link back to #28020.

@@ -510,10 +510,35 @@ class ServerArgs:
                 'Which model-config parser to use. "auto" picks "mistral" '
                 'via the is_mistral_model name heuristic, else "hf" '
                 "(AutoConfig over config.json). Plugins can register additional "
-                "parsers via @register_model_config_parser."
+                "parsers via @register_model_config_parser. See also "
+                "--config-format (vLLM-style alias)."
             )
         ),
     ] = "auto"
+    # Implemented as a separate field (rather than an
+    # Arg(aliases=["--config-format"]) on model_config_parser) so that
+    # passing both flags with conflicting values raises an error instead of
+    # silently letting whichever flag appears last on the command line win;
+    # see _handle_config_format().
+    config_format: A[
+        Optional[str],
+        Arg(
+            help=(
+                "vLLM-style alias for --model-config-parser. Accepts the same "
+                'values ("auto", "hf", "mistral", or any plugin-registered '
+                "parser name; matching is case- and whitespace-insensitive). "
+                "If --model-config-parser is also explicitly set to a "
+                "different value, this raises an error rather than silently "
+                'picking one -- "auto" is compared like any other explicit '
+                "value, so e.g. --config-format=auto together with an "
+                "explicit --model-config-parser=hf also raises. If "
+                "--config-format=mistral and --load-format is left at its "
+                'default, --load-format is also set to "mistral" so '
+                "vLLM-style Mistral invocations (--config-format mistral "
+                "--load-format mistral) work verbatim on SGLang."
+            )
+        ),
+    ] = None
     json_model_override_args: A[
         str,
         "A dictionary in JSON string format used to override default model configurations.",
@@ -2634,6 +2659,11 @@ def __post_init__(self):
         self._validate_prefill_only_disable_kv_cache_args()
         self._handle_dcp_validation()
 
+        # Reconcile the vLLM-style --config-format alias with
+        # --model-config-parser before the dummy-model short-circuit below,
+        # so a conflicting-flags mistake is caught even for dummy/none models.
+        self._handle_config_format()
+
         if self.model_path.lower() in ["none", "dummy"]:
             # Skip for dummy models
             return
@@ -5487,6 +5517,34 @@ def _resolve_storage_layout_compatibility(self):
             f"switching to {new_layout} layout for {self.hicache_io_backend} io backend"
         )
 
+    def _handle_config_format(self):
+        # --config-format is the vLLM-style alias for --model-config-parser.
+        # If the user passed the alias, it takes precedence. Erroring on
+        # simultaneous conflicting values is more useful than silently
+        # picking a winner.
+        if self.config_format is None:
+            return
+        self.config_format = self.config_format.strip().lower()
+        if not self.config_format:
+            # "" / whitespace-only is treated the same as not passing the flag.
+            return
+        if (
+            self.model_config_parser.lower() != "auto"
+            and self.model_config_parser.lower() != self.config_format
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"--config-format={self.config_format!r} conflicts with "
+                f"--model-config-parser={self.model_config_parser!r}. "
+                "Pass only one."
+            )
+        self.model_config_parser = self.config_format
+        # vLLM-style invocations often pass --load-format mistral explicitly,
+        # but when they don't, the alias's "mistral" choice should still
+        # drive weight loading -- unless the user already picked a different
+        # load format explicitly.
+        if self.config_format == "mistral" and self.load_format == "auto":
+            self.load_format = "mistral"
+
     def _handle_load_format(self):

         # (arg_groups/overrides.py: _gguf_quantization); load_format itself is

@@ -204,8 +204,10 @@ def get_config(
     if is_gguf:

             raise ValueError(
-                f"model_config_parser={model_config_parser!r} is incompatible "

             )
         _ensure_gguf_version()
         kwargs["gguf_file"] = model

@@ -1336,5 +1336,104 @@ def test_token_oracle_accepted_when_env_enabled(self):
         self.assertEqual(parsed.sampling_backend, "token_oracle")
 
 
+class TestConfigFormatAlias(CustomTestCase):
+    """--config-format is a vLLM-parity alias for --model-config-parser.
+
+    Tests the reconciliation function _handle_config_format directly on a
+    minimal SimpleNamespace stand-in for ServerArgs -- this isolates the
+    reconciliation states without going through prepare_server_args, which
+    would try to actually load a model config (and would rightly fail for a
+    non-Mistral model when config_format='mistral' is set).
+    """
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _reconcile(config_format, model_config_parser, load_format="auto"):
+        from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+
+        ns = SimpleNamespace(
+            config_format=config_format,
+            model_config_parser=model_config_parser,
+            load_format=load_format,
+        )
+        ServerArgs._handle_config_format(ns)
+        return ns
+
+    def test_neither_flag_leaves_default(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(config_format=None, model_config_parser="auto")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.model_config_parser, "auto")
+        self.assertIsNone(ns.config_format)
+
+    def test_config_format_propagates_to_parser(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(config_format="mistral", model_config_parser="auto")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.model_config_parser, "mistral")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.config_format, "mistral")
+
+    def test_conflicting_flags_error(self):
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "conflicts with"):
+            self._reconcile(config_format="mistral", model_config_parser="hf")
+
+    def test_matching_flags_accepted(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(config_format="mistral", model_config_parser="mistral")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.model_config_parser, "mistral")
+
+    def test_explicit_auto_config_format_conflicts_like_any_other_value(self):
+        # "auto" is compared as a literal value on the config_format side,
+        # same as "hf"/"mistral"/etc -- it is only treated as "not set" on
+        # the model_config_parser side (the default). This is intentional:
+        # an explicit --config-format=auto together with an explicit,
+        # different --model-config-parser is a real, reportable conflict.
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "conflicts with"):
+            self._reconcile(config_format="auto", model_config_parser="hf")
+
+    def test_config_format_case_and_whitespace_normalized(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(config_format="  Mistral  ", model_config_parser="auto")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.model_config_parser, "mistral")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.config_format, "mistral")
+
+    def test_config_format_case_insensitive_matches_parser(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(config_format="Mistral", model_config_parser="mistral")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.model_config_parser, "mistral")
+
+    def test_empty_config_format_is_noop(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(config_format="", model_config_parser="hf")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.model_config_parser, "hf")
+
+    def test_whitespace_only_config_format_is_noop(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(config_format="   ", model_config_parser="hf")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.model_config_parser, "hf")
+
+    def test_config_format_mistral_sets_load_format_when_auto(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(config_format="mistral", model_config_parser="auto")
+        self.assertEqual(ns.load_format, "mistral")
+
+    def test_config_format_mistral_does_not_override_explicit_load_format(self):
+        ns = self._reconcile(
+            config_format="mistral",
+            model_config_parser="auto",
+            load_format="safetensors",
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(ns.load_format, "safetensors")
+
+    def test_dummy_model_path_still_validates_config_format(self):
+        # Regression test: _handle_config_format() must run before the
+        # dummy/none model_path short-circuit in __post_init__, so a
+        # conflicting-flags mistake is still caught for dummy models.
+        from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "conflicts with"):
+            ServerArgs(
+                model_path="dummy",
+                config_format="mistral",
+                model_config_parser="hf",
+            )
+
+        server_args = ServerArgs(
+            model_path="dummy",
+            config_format="mistral",
+            model_config_parser="auto",
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(server_args.model_config_parser, "mistral")
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
